observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a full-length mirror wall on the left, draped gray curtains, a wooden ballet barre, a wall-mounted fan, a standing fan and a potted plant. A woman seen from behind (white spaghetti-strap tank top, loose pink pants, hair in a bun with a clip) stands center-right with both arms extended overhead; her front-view reflection appears in the mirror on the left. The two figures are the same person and her mirror image, not two dancers.
visible_changes: Over frames 1-3 she stands on both feet with arms straight overhead; from frame 4 onward one leg bends and the foot lifts off the floor into a retiré/passé position behind the standing knee (mirrored as an extended back leg in the reflection).
Frames 11-20 she rises onto the ball of the standing foot (relevé), heel off the floor, while keeping the working foot tucked behind the knee and arms overhead.

Frames 21-29 her torso and hips rotate so more of her right side is visible; the arms reshape from straight-up to a curved overhead pose, and the working foot moves from behind toward the front of the standing knee.
Frames 30-34 she lowers the working leg out to a wide stance/lunge as the body turns further, and the arms sweep down from overhead to a curved mid-level position.
Frames 35-41 she settles into a wider two-foot stance facing more toward the mirror, arms continuing to lower and open to the sides; the reflection tracks all of these changes.
The background (curtains, fans, mirror seams) drifts steadily to the right across the frames, indicating a slow camera pan/drift rather than the dancer translating through the room.
outside_clip_unknowns: The onset of the overhead arm position and the initial two-foot stance are already in progress at the crop start.
What follows the final lowered-arm, wide-stance position (recovery, next step, or end of phrase) is not shown.
Whether the turn is part of a larger choreography sequence is unknown.
uncertain_details: Exact axis/direction of the body turn is hard to pin down because she is viewed from behind and the camera also drifts.
Camera motion is a slow pan/possible slight zoom; the dancer's apparent rightward shift in frame is largely camera-induced, not locomotion.
The moment the working foot leaves the floor and the moment it lands in the wide stance are gradual and not sharply defined between sampled frames.
